goal: One narrow governance correction from canonical main 37c0ee06e81c044a3e6ba5501301ae84db02e87b in milestone_contracts/governance/career-os-document-rendering-capability-v1-contract.json correcting the composition of TAG_SEQUENCE_GENERATOR_V1 (tag_model.generator). The canonical text fed the full ordered platform_sequence S to both cpython_tags and compatible_tags and stated that this is the composition sys_tags() performs for CPython. On the pinned stack (interpreter /usr/local/python/3.14.2/bin/python3.14, installer pip 26.2.1) S contains the universal platform `any` (its last entry), and the canonical generator yields 1240 tags where the actual pinned sys_tags() yields 1226: the 14 additional tags are spurious CPython `*-any` tags generated by passing `any` to cpython_tags. The corrected rule: S_cpython = [p for p in S if p != 'any'] (original relative order of every remaining platform preserved); tag_sequence = list(cpython_tags(python_version=(X, Y), abis=[A], platforms=S_cpython)) followed by list(compatible_tags(python_version=(X, Y), interpreter='cp<X><Y>', platforms=S_cpython)), then the existing rendering and de-duplication. The literal platform `any` is excluded from the platform list given to BOTH functions, because compatible_tags itself generates every -none-any tag; the variant that excludes `any` only from cpython_tags and gives the full S to compatible_tags was measured on the pinned stack and does NOT reproduce sys_tags() (same 1226-tag set but 602 tags displaced, with py*-none-any emitted inside the platform loop and cp314-none-any last). No other TAG_MODEL_V1, platform_sequence, platform_tags, ordering, compatibility, wheel-priority, hosted-target, dependency, renderer, E2 helper-chain or gate semantics change. No implementation, verifier, provisioning-script, manifest, dependency, installation, provisioning, release, merge or submission authority is created.

Pinned measurements on BUILDER_DEV with the interpreter and pip 26.2.1 named in the goal: platform_sequence S has 40 entries with `any` last; actual sys_tags() = 1226 tags; the previous canonical generator = 1240 tags, the 14 additional being CPython `*-any` tags (cp314-cp314-any, cp314-abi3-any, cp313-abi3-any, cp312-abi3-any, cp311-abi3-any, cp310-abi3-any and the abi3 and cp314 variants after them); the implementation and verifier followed the canonical text literally, so this is a canonical specification defect, not an implementation divergence.

CORRECTED RULE: for a CPython target with (X, Y), abi_tag A and ordered platform_sequence S, S_cpython = [p for p in S if p != 'any'] preserving the original relative order of all remaining platforms; tag_sequence = list(cpython_tags(python_version=(X, Y), abis=[A], platforms=S_cpython)) followed by list(compatible_tags(python_version=(X, Y), interpreter='cp<X><Y>', platforms=S_cpython)); the two yielded sequences are concatenated in that order and later duplicates are removed exactly as before. The corrected generator on the pinned stack yields exactly the 1226-tag actual sys_tags() sequence, in the same order.

REJECTED VARIANT (measured, not adopted): giving the full S including `any` to compatible_tags while excluding `any` only from cpython_tags yields the same set of 1226 tags but not the same sequence: 602 tags are displaced, the first difference is at index 624 (sys_tags() has py3-none-manylinux_2_39_x86_64 where this variant has py314-none-any), and the variant ends with cp314-none-any instead of py30-none-any. The reason is the documented behavior of compatible_tags, which iterates the given platforms for py*-none-<platform> and itself yields <interpreter>-none-any and py*-none-any after them, so `any` inside its platform list produces py*-none-any tags out of position. Selection order is selection-relevant under TAG_MODEL_V1, so this variant is not a faithful reproduction of sys_tags() and would fail the TAG_GENERATOR SELF-CHECK.
